brief: JPM's afternoon update reports a broad equity rally (65% of stocks higher, 10 of 11 sectors green, long buying plus short covering) alongside today's ISM-Srvcs release: final PMI revised up to 58.8 (highest since July 2021), consistent with ~5% annualized Sept GDP growth per the release, versus JPM's 3.5% forecast; the separate ISM services index eased to 54.9 but new orders stayed elevated at 59.8 and prices paid jumped to 74.0, the highest since July 2022, a component JPM says leads CPI by 2-3 months and remains a key inflation risk. JPM reiterates its Tactically Bullish stance (set last week on improving macro, consumer strength, earnings expectations, stabilizing yields, technicals), arguing higher yields keep concentrating gains in Tech and that Cyclicals need yields to stabilize or fall; it favors Financials ex-Tech (light positioning) and keeps Tech as a core long without an RTY pair given squeeze risk. Desk commentary: a long/short in regional and money-center banks (long C/MS/PNC/FITB/CFG/BNY, short WFC/TFC/RF/BAC/HBAN); Brazil upgraded to Overweight after first-round election results, with MSCI Brazil seen gaining 12% near-term, rising to 20%; a Delta-One note warns a rising Stagflation factor and rolling-over growth surprises could turn into a tech headwind.
